title:
Assessing sensitivity to semantic and syntactic information in deaf readers: An ERP
study
description: This dataset contains EEG recordings from deaf readers who read sentences containing semantic and syntactic violations, used to assess sensitivity to semantic and syntactic information during reading. Event-related potentials were recorded while participants viewed 180 sentences presented word by word, including subject-verb agreement, semantic, double, and word-order violations alongside correct control sentences.
methods_description: Data were collected at the NeuroCognition Laboratory in San Diego. Participants sat in a darkened, sound-attenuated room and viewed sentences on an LCD monitor. Sentences were presented in an RSVP design, one word at a time for 600 ms with a 200 ms ISI. There were 180 sentences: 30 each of subject-verb agreement, semantic, double, and word-order violations, plus 60 correct controls. Participants responded with a keyboard, and verbal responses were recorded through a headset.
